summary: MIT founded April 10 1861 under Massachusetts charter two days before Civil War started. William Barton Rogers proposed a new kind of institution blending science and industry. First building in Boston's Back Bay. Moved to Cambridge 1916. Motto Mens et Manus (Mind and Hand) reflects applied science philosophy.

MIT Radiation Laboratory 1940-1945: developed radar for WWII. 4000 staff, $2B budget (equivalent to $30B today). Developed microwave radar, LORAN navigation, fire control systems. 1/3 of all US physicists worked there. Spun off into Lincoln Lab 1951. Rad Lab work shortened WWII and saved millions of lives.

Whirlwind computer at MIT 1948-1951: first real-time digital computer. Built for flight simulator. Jay Forrester invented magnetic core memory for it. 2048x2048 pixel display. SAGE air defense system was based on Whirlwind. Core memory became world standard for 20 years. Whirlwind shaped computing's direction for decades.

Project MAC at MIT 1963: Multiple Access Computer. Funded by ARPA. Time-sharing system let multiple users work simultaneously. Marvin Minsky led AI Lab. Fernando Corbató led Multics. Project MAC became Laboratory for Computer Science (LCS) 1976. Merged with AI Lab 2003 as CSAIL.

MIT AI Lab founded 1959 by Marvin Minsky and John McCarthy. Early work: blocks world vision, SHRDLU natural language, Logo programming for children, Society of Mind theory. Seymour Papert, Gerald Sussman, Patrick Winston. MIT was one of four original AI centers with Stanford, CMU, and IBM. PDP model of mind originated here.

MIT AI Lab culture birthed open source. Richard Stallman MIT AI Lab 1971-1983. Founded GNU Project 1983 and Free Software Foundation 1985 after lab culture collapsed. GNU Emacs, GCC, GPL license. Linus Torvalds wrote Linux kernel 1991 using GNU tools. MIT hackers created the template for open collaboration.

MIT Media Lab founded 1985 by Nicholas Negroponte and Jerome Wiesner. Anti-disciplinary research: wearables, tangible bits, one laptop per child, Scratch programming. Funded by corporate consortium not grants. 80+ research groups. Known for demo-driven culture: show not tell. 30 years of demos that became products.

MIT CSAIL (Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Lab) formed 2003 merging LCS and AI Lab. 700+ members, 100+ principal investigators. Largest CS lab at MIT. Birthplace of RSA encryption, Ethernet, GNU, World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), Kerberos, spreadsheets, parallel computing. 10 Turing Awards from CSAIL lineage.

RSA encryption invented at MIT 1977 by Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir, Leonard Adleman. Public-key cryptosystem based on factoring difficulty. RSA-129 challenge took 17 years to factor. RSA underpins HTTPS, SSH, PGP, digital signatures. Three founders started RSA Security. Turing Award 2002. Most influential cryptography invention in history.

Ethernet invented by Bob Metcalfe at Xerox PARC 1973 while on leave from MIT. MIT thesis on packet switching informed design. 10 Mbps over coaxial cable. Metcalfe founded 3Com 1979. Ethernet became IEEE 802.3 standard 1983. Now runs at 400 Gbps. Every internet connection traces through Ethernet frames. MIT alumni shaped networking's foundation.

W3C (World Wide Web Consortium) hosted at MIT LCS 1994-2023 under Tim Berners-Lee. Set HTML, CSS, XML, SVG, Web Accessibility standards. MIT moved W3C to joint MIT/ERCIM/Keio management. W3C ensured web stayed open and interoperable. CSS working group at MIT defined how every web page looks.

MIT OpenCourseWare launched 2002: free online materials for 2,500+ MIT courses. 400 million visitors. Started open education movement. Inspired edX 2012 with Harvard and Berkeley. edX acquired by 2U 2021 for $800M. MIT OCW remains free. Demonstrated that open sharing of knowledge scales education globally.

One Laptop Per Child (OLPC) launched at MIT Media Lab 2005 by Nicholas Negroponte. Goal: $100 laptop for developing world education. Distributed 2.4M laptops in Uruguay, Peru, Rwanda, Afghanistan. XO laptop: dual mode screen, hand crank power, mesh networking. Commercially unsuccessful but influenced netbook category and low-cost computing movement.

MIT Lincoln Lab founded 1951 as federally funded R&D center. Air defense, space surveillance, laser communication, cyber security. Operates 18+ programs for DoD and DHS. 4000 staff, $1B+ annual budget. Developed SAGE, spaced-based early warning, lasercom. Lincoln Lab is MIT's defense applied research arm, classified work outside main campus.

MIT AI history spans decades: Minsky's Society of Mind, Winston's thesis on learning, Brooks' behavior-based robotics, Picard's affective computing, Torralba's massive data, Tenenbaum's probabilistic models. MIT contributed to every wave: symbolic, connectionist, deep learning. MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab founded 2017 with $240M 10-year commitment for hybrid cloud AI research.

Scratch programming language developed at MIT Media Lab 2003-2007 by Mitchel Resnick's Lifelong Kindergarten group. Visual block-based programming for children ages 8-16. 100M+ projects shared. Available in 60+ languages. Inspired ScratchJr for younger children and App Inventor for mobile. Demonstrated that programming can be accessible to all ages.

Scratch 3.0 2019 added extensions: LEGO WeDo, micro:bit, LEGO Mindstorms, translate, text-to-speech, video sensing. Allows connecting physical devices to Scratch programs. Demonstrates MIT's approach to bridging digital and physical worlds. Scratch extensions ecosystem grew to 30+ official extensions.

MIT motto Mens et Manus (Mind and Hand) reflects founding philosophy: science should serve practical purpose. MIT requires lab work, projects, hands-on learning for all students. UROP (Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program) since 1969: 90% of undergraduates participate in research. Distinguishes MIT from pure-theory institutions.

MIT alumni founded companies that would rank as 11th largest economy in world. 30,000+ active companies, $2 trillion annual revenue. Akamai, Bose, Dropbox, iRobot, Khan Academy, Intel cofounder Robert Noyce. MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition since 1989. MIT Sandbox Innovation Fund provides $1M/year to student projects. MIT is engine of startup creation.

MIT has strongest maker culture in academia. Hobby Shop since 1938. MITERS student-run electronics shop. MakerLodge, MIT Mini Maker Faire. 3D printing, laser cutting, PCB milling available to all students. Project-based culture: 2.007 robotics competition, 6.111 digital systems lab, Mystery Hunt. Building things is central to MIT identity, not optional extracurricular.

Ian Osgood's 1966 MIT thesis on pattern recognition: explored early character recognition using statistical methods. Part of Project MAC and AI Lab lineage. Contemporary with Marvin Minsky's work. Demonstrates MIT's long commitment to machine learning research from the earliest days of the field, decades before deep learning made it mainstream.

MIT 6.001 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (SICP) taught 1980-2009. Book by Abelson and Sussman used worldwide. Taught Scheme/Lisp as vehicle for abstraction, data, state, metalinguistic concepts. Considered one of most influential CS textbooks. MIT replaced 6.001 with Python-based 6.01 in 2009, controversial change.

Project Athena 1983-1991: MIT IBM DEC partnership for distributed computing on campus. 1000 Unix workstations in classrooms and dorms. Developed X Window System, Kerberos authentication, Zephyr messaging. Demonstrated client-server computing at scale for education. X Window System from Athena runs on every Linux desktop today.

MIT Technology Licensing Office (TLO) founded 1986. 700+ patents, 200+ startups spun out, $1B+ in cumulative royalties. Model: MIT does not hold patents for blocking competitors, only for enabling commercialization. Takes equity instead of upfront fees. MIT's approach influenced Bayh-Dole Act implementation nationwide for university tech transfer.

MIT is leading quantum research university. MIT quantum faculty: Peter Shor (Shor's factoring algorithm), Seth Lloyd (quantum computing), William Oliver (superconducting qubits). MIT Lincoln Lab operates quantum testbeds. MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab does quantum machine learning. MIT launched Quantum Engineering program 2020.

Tim Berners-Lee at MIT started Solid Project 2015: decentralized web where users control their data. Pod architecture: personal data stores, apps must ask permission. Inrupt company founded 2018 to commercialize. Berners-Lee received Turing Award 2017. Solid challenges Web 2.0 centralized model of Facebook Google Amazon controlling user data.

MIT CSAIL 5G and 6G research: full-duplex radio (transmit and receive simultaneously same frequency), massive MIMO optimization, terahertz communication. 6G target: 1 Tbps, sub-millisecond latency. MIT's approach focuses on physical layer innovations rather than network architecture. Collaborates with Nokia Bell Labs and NTT.

MIT climate research spans Joint Program on Science and Policy of Global Change (founded 1991), Energy Initiative (MITEI 2006), Climate Modeling Initiative. MIT Integrated Global System Model (IGSM) used by IPCC. Nuclear fusion: MIT SPARC tokamak with Commonwealth Fusion Systems, aiming for net energy by 2025. MIT commits to carbon neutrality by 2026.

MIT nanotechnology research: quantum dots, carbon nanotubes, 2D materials, self-assembly. MIT.nano facility opened 2018: 200,000 sq ft cleanroom and characterization labs, largest at any university. Strano Research Group: nanotube sensors, plants as chemical detectors. MIT nanomedicine: drug delivery, imaging contrast agents. MIT is a top nanotechnology research institution worldwide.

MIT defense research: Lincoln Lab ($1B+ annual), CSAIL cyber security for DoD, Institute for Soldier Nanotechnologies, DARPA contracts across multiple departments. MIT research has contributed to SAGE, radar, GPS modernization, drone technology, cybersecurity standards. MIT has historically maintained defense research relationships despite student protests in 1960s-70s over Vietnam and classified work.

MIT modern CS curriculum reorganized 2020s: 6.100 series for fundamentals (Python-based), 6.200 series for systems, 6.3000 series for AI/ML. 6.S081 (formerly 6.828) operating systems uses RISC-V and xv6. 6.S192 deep learning. 6.S191 introduction to deep learning lectures available online with millions of views. MIT curriculum stays current with industry demands.
